components.note: 日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'
⺮ (bamboo) — ancient texts were written on bound bamboo strips, and 第 originally referred to the sequential order of such strips, giving rise to its meaning 'ordinal number' (as in 第一, first).
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
犭 (dog/animal) — historically linked to a wary, hesitant animal, extended to mean 'as if, similar to.'
尤 (yóu) is an exact match for the sound of 犹.
太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'
木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo
士 (a scholar/gentleman) — represents a person of learning and ambition.
心 (heart/mind) — the mind and aspirations of a scholar gave 志 its meaning 'purpose, will, ambition.'
虫 (insect) — 蜘 (as in 蜘蛛, spider) names a small crawling creature.
知 (zhī) gives the sound — an exact match with 蜘's reading.
虫 (insect) — 蛛 names a small creature, the spider.
朱 (zhū) gives the sound — an exact match with 蛛.
犭 (dog/animal) — 狗 names an animal, the dog.
句 (jù) gives a sound distantly related to gǒu, having drifted apart over time.
尸 (body) — 屁 relates to a bodily function.
比 (bǐ) gives a sound only distantly related to pì today, having drifted apart over time.
汉 is a simplified form of 漢, pairing the water radical 氵 with a component that named the river valley tied to the Han dynasty and Han Chinese identity.
保 (to protect) — 堡 describes a structure built for defense.
土 (earth) — earthen 土 walls built for defense 保 gave 堡 its meaning 'fort, fortress.'

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 急 relates to an anxious or urgent state of mind
刍 (chú) gives a sound distantly related to 急's reading jí, having drifted apart over time
冫 (water/ice) — 冲 relates to liquid, as in pouring or rinsing with water
中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to 冲's reading chōng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time
天 (sky, standing in for the ruler above) suggests something reported upward to the emperor, the root of 奏's old meaning 'to present a memorial.'
木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
宀 (roof) — 富 relates to a well-stocked household, prosperous under its own roof
畐 (fú) gives a sound close to 富's reading fù, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
予 (to give) — 幻 is drawn as an inverted, mirror-image form of 予, picturing something turned upside down or not as it seems, giving 幻 its meaning 'illusion, fantasy.'
见 (to see, perceive) — relates to 觉's meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive.'
⺍ is a small graphic element serving as the phonetic hint, though its link to jué's modern sound has faded after centuries of change.
圭, made of two 土 (earth) stacked together, depicts a handful of mortar or soil.
寸 (a hand/small measure) — sealing something shut with packed mortar gave 封 its meaning 'to seal, to close.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赚 relates to earning money.
兼 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to 赚's reading zhuàn, having drifted apart over time.
钅 (metal) — 钱 relates to money, since early Chinese coins were made of metal
戋 (jiān) gives a loose sound connection to 钱's reading qián
冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.
俞 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tōu, having drifted apart over time.

艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match
乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time
平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.
扌 (hand) — 按 relates to pressing something with the hand
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 按's reading àn, differing only in tone
手 (hand) — 摩 describes rubbing something with the hand.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.

身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.
疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating
犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time
女 (woman) — 奴 originally described a woman kept as a servant in a household.
又 (a hand) — standing beside the master's hand 又, the woman 女 gave 奴 its meaning 'slave, servant.'
A hand shape.
Represents grain being handled, linked to labor and servitude.
走 (to walk, to run) — 赶 relates to pursuing or hurrying, both forms of movement.
干 (gān) gives a rhyme close to gǎn, with the tone shifted.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
口 (mouth) — 吓 relates to a shout or cry, as when someone is frightened.
下 (xià) gives the sound — an exact match with 吓.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
木 (wood) — early spears and rifle stocks were made of wood.
仓 (cāng) gives a sound close to qiāng, sharing the same rhyme.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
辶 (to walk) shows movement.
万 (ten thousand, suggesting a great distance) shows a big stride, giving 迈 its meaning 'to step, to stride.'
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
力 (strength/effort) — the exertion behind the achievement.
工 (work/labor) — results produced through skillful labor, giving 功 its meaning 'achievement, merit, skill.'
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'
木 (tree/wood) — many early villages were built among or from trees and wood
寸 (cùn) gives a sound close to 村's reading cūn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
宀 (roof/house) — relates to 完's meaning 'complete, finish,' as in a fully built house.

敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'

稣 (sū) gives the sound — 苏 is also pronounced sū, an exact match
木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.

邦 (a nation/state) — a community bound together
巾 (a flag/cloth) — a banner people rally around to support one another

亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
